title: Aaron Sorkin Omits Trump from January 6 Capitol Riot Film
text:
Director Aaron Sorkin says he left Donald Trump's name out of his January 6 Capitol riot film to avoid making it too political, focusing instead on Facebook's role.
Director Aaron Sorkin has confirmed that his upcoming film about the January 6 Capitol Hill riot does not mention President Donald Trump by name, despite the event being a central topic. In an interview with Politico, Sorkin said he made the choice to keep the film from becoming too political. The film also examines Facebook's role in the 2020 election and the subsequent scrutiny the company faced in 2021.
Sorkin Explains Decision to Omit Trump
Sorkin told Politico that he did not want the film to be overly political, even though its subject matter is inherently charged. He stated that leaving Trump's name out would keep the film clean of excessive political baggage. Sorkin said he was not given a directive by the studio but made the call himself.
He recalled telling Sony Pictures chairman Tom Rothman that the sequence would not feature any Trump signage or red hats. Instead, the scene includes symbols such as Don't Tread on Me flags, Stop the Steal signs, American flags, and Confederate flags. Sorkin emphasized that the film would not frame the events as MAGA versus everybody else or even red versus blue.
According to Sorkin, the focus is on Facebook's role in the rise of divisiveness, extremism, and hyperpartisanship. He explained that as soon as the scene included anything Trump-related, it would become about something else. He added that he prefers to have clean hands, acknowledging that the film may still be perceived as political.
Facebook's Role in the 2020 Election
The film follows Facebook's alleged part in spreading misinformation during the 2020 election cycle. It is not known whether Sorkin will address claims that Facebook chief Mark Zuckerberg worked with the Biden administration to shut down conservative content creators and violate their freedom of speech. Those claims remain unverified.
Sorkin's film may face challenges at the box office. According to Christian Toto, the film The Social Network carried a $40 million budget. If this follow-up has a similar production cost, it may struggle to make back its budget.
Political Themes and Box Office Prospects
Sorkin's decision to avoid Trump's name is unusual given the film's subject matter. The January 6 riot was a highly political event, and the film's exploration of Facebook's role adds another layer of political complexity. By excluding direct references to Trump, Sorkin aims to keep the narrative focused on broader issues of extremism and divisiveness.
The film industry often sees political films struggle commercially, especially when they are perceived as taking a strong partisan stance. Sorkin's attempt to remain neutral may be a strategic move to appeal to a wider audience. However, the film's success will depend on how it balances its political themes with engaging storytelling.
As of now, no release date has been announced for the film. Sorkin's comments have sparked discussion about the role of politics in cinema and the challenges of depicting recent historical events.
